heard: Saturn's giant rings formed while dinosaurs roamed Earth. Astronomers long assumed the solar system's widest rings were ancient. Math in the late 1850s proved they were icy particles. NASA's Cassini spacecraft changed everything during its final dives. It skimmed between Saturn and its rings to measure their gravity. The pole was far too weak for an ancient structure. Cassini's low mass measurement proved the rings are remarkably young. A shattered icy moon created them only recently. Early dinosaurs lived under a completely ringless night sky.
